name: Exposure to Suicide and Self-Harm — 5-indicator study-aligned checklist
construct: Exposure to self-harm and suicidal behaviour among family and close friends
participant_measure: Study-aligned exposure checklist derived from Scottish Wellbeing Study reporting
range: Five separate binary indicators; optional any-exposure composite 0/1
rights: Research-derived contextual indicators. Wording is a transparent study-aligned reconstruction based on published construct descriptions and examples; it is not represented as verbatim Scottish Wellbeing Study questionnaire wording.
evidence: De Beurs et al. (2019) reports five items assessing whether friends or family had self-harmed, attempted suicide, or died by suicide, dichotomised no/yes. Wetherall et al. (2018) reports friend suicide attempt, family suicide attempt, and family/friend suicide death as distinct exposure variables. Later Scottish Wellbeing Study work reports exposure to close others' NSSI, suicide attempt, and suicide death.
audit: Study-aligned reconstruction; exact original five-item questionnaire wording not claimed

items.text: Has anyone among your family deliberately harmed themselves?
Has anyone among your close friends deliberately harmed themselves?
Has anyone among your family attempted suicide?
Has anyone among your close friends attempted suicide?
Has anyone among your family or close friends died by suicide?

scoring.method: Preserve all five indicators separately. An optional descriptive any-exposure composite may be coded 1 if any item is endorsed and 0 otherwise, matching the dichotomisation described by De Beurs et al. (2019).

safety_note: Exposure history is contextual information and is not an individual suicide-risk probability. No pattern of responses establishes that a participant is safe or unsafe.
